title: Chronic adversity and cerebellar structure: Links with neighborhood disadvantage and childhood maltreatment in adult trauma survivors.
summary: Chronic adversity, including neighborhood socioeconomic disadvantage and childhood maltreatment, has been linked to alterations in brain structure and increased risk for psychopathology. While prior research has focused largely on cortical and limbic regions, the cerebellum is increasingly recognized for its role in cognitive and affective processes and may be particularly sensitive to prolonged stress. The present study examined associations between chronic adversity and cerebellar volume in a sample of trauma-exposed adults. title: A benchmarking framework for organoid computing.
summary: Organoid computing leverages functional neural networks of lab-grown neural organoids to recapitulate key aspects of human brain information processing, holding promising potential in brain-inspired computing, brain-computer interfaces, neuroscience, and medicine. However, its broad application remains constrained due to technical limitations including biological variability, interface instability, stochastic performance, and limited reproducibility. Here, we present a benchmarking framework that systematically quantifies the key performance determinants of organoid computing. title: Direction-specific effects of biphasic transcranial magnetic stimulation on cortical and cortico-spinal excitability.
summary: Transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) is a well-established tool for inducing cortical excitation. However, the relevance of current direction on elicited effects is still incompletely understood. Combining TMS with electroencephalography (EEG) and electromyography (EMG) enables non-invasive analysis of evoked potentials both on cortical and peripheral level. summary: Viral encephalitis, meningitis, and myelitis are rare but life-threatening complications after autologous or allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation (HSCT) and chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy, associated with 30-60% mortality and frequent neurological sequelae. The absence of harmonised definitions and diagnostic criteria contributes to delayed diagnosis, underreporting, and substantial heterogeneity across centres. summary: We report a 44-year-old man with a non-functioning pituitary macroadenoma diagnosed approximately 10 years before the current presentation. He subsequently developed metastatic amelanotic melanoma originating from a cutaneous lesion of the right auricle, with jejunal metastases. After disease progression despite immunotherapy and chemotherapy, he presented with visual disturbances and panhypopituitarism. title: Multimodal Assessment of the Effects of Acute Alcohol Intake on Resting-State Neural Function.

summary: Combined neuroimaging modalities may clarify the mechanisms underlying alcohol's acute neurobehavioral effects. Past studies have typically focused on blood oxygen level-dependent (BOLD) correlates of alcohol-induced impairment. In this report, we integrated magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS), arterial spin labeling (ASL), and BOLD functional magnetic resonance imaging metrics to identify the mechanisms underlying acute alcohol effects on the anterior cingulate cortex (ACC), given its critical role in attention, inhibition, and affect. title: MYCN-amplified spinal ependymoma: a three-patient case series and focussed literature review.
summary: MYCN-amplified spinal ependymomas are a rare, recently described aggressive subtype of ependymoma defined by molecular profiling. We present three cases: a 52-year-old man, a 37-year-old woman, and a 28-year-old man presented with progressive neurological symptoms and spinal cord lesions identified on magnetic resonance imaging. These cases demonstrate the challenges in radiological identification and the importance of histological and molecular profiling to guide aggressive treatment of MYCN-amplified spinal ependymomas including surgical resection, radiotherapy, and chemotherapy. title: An Incidental Discovery of Multiple Sclerosis in an 18-Year-Old Male Following Posttraumatic Brain Imaging.
summary: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a chronic, debilitating autoimmune disease for which there is currently no cure. Most commonly, MS presents in white, middle-aged females. However, the pathogenesis of the condition is incompletely understood. We report a rare case of the incidental discovery of MS in an 18-year-old male. In-depth neurological workup following traumatic brain injury secondary to a motor vehicle accident revealed nonenhancing demyelinating lesions in the brain and spine on MRI. Further workup, including CSF positivity for oligoclonal bands, supported the diagnosis of MS, and the patient promptly began disease-modifying therapy (DMT) with ocrelizumab. title: Loneliness and the social brain: the mediating role of social functioning between nucleus accumbens structure and loneliness in aging.
summary: Loneliness is a complex and distressing emotional state linked to impaired health and well-being in later life. Although its behavioral and social correlates are well documented, the neural mechanisms underlying loneliness remain less clear. The nucleus accumbens (NAcc) plays a central role in reward processing and social motivation, suggesting its potential involvement in loneliness. The present study examined whether individual differences in loneliness are associated with structural variation in the NAcc, and whether social functioning mediates this relationship. title: Neurophysiological evidence for rapid semantic integration via fast mapping.
summary: Theories of declarative memory consolidation hold that novel associative information is integrated into cortical semantic networks slowly and with hippocampal support. However, an encoding paradigm called fast mapping (FM) has been proposed to permit rapid cortical integration of novel item-label associations, particularly when the novel item shares substantial visual-semantic features with a simultaneously presented known concept. title: Diagnostic accuracy and reliability of susceptibility map-weighted imaging in patients with clinically uncertain parkinsonian syndromes.
summary: Parkinson's disease (PD) is characterized by degeneration of dopaminergic neurons in the substantia nigra, accompanied by increased iron accumulation, particularly in the nigrosome-1 subregion. Differentiating neurodegenerative disorders like PD from non-neurodegenerative causes of parkinsonism can be challenging. In clinically uncertain parkinsonian syndrome (CUPS), dopamine transporter (DAT)-single-photon emission computed tomography (SPECT) can aid diagnosis. Previous neuroimaging research has primarily focused on the salience network, with limited attention to the dorsal attention network. title: Tensor-based dynamic MRI reconstruction with non-convex ℓrp pseudo-norm and adaptive weighting.
summary: Compressed sensing significantly accelerates dynamic magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) by undersampling (k, t)-space, thereby formulating an ill-posed inverse problem that heavily depends on reconstruction algorithms. Dynamic MRI data exhibit low-rank property due to strong correlations in both spatial and temporal dimensions. In this paper, we propose a tensor-based ℓrp pseudo-norm regularization for low-rank dynamic MRI reconstruction model, and introduce the weighting mechanism to adaptively distinguish between signal and noise, termed as TNWLR. title: The impaired white matter integrity and altered functional connectivity in Parkinson's disease.
summary: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a neurodegenerative disorder characterized by structural abnormalities in the cerebral cortex and subcortical regions. Nevertheless, functional connectivity (FC) alterations within these affected white matter (WM) regions have not been fully clarified. We combine diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) and resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (rs-fMRI) to explore abnormalities in WM structure and FC in 20 PD patients and 22 age- and gender-matched healthy controls (HCs). title: Longitudinal association between baseline brain entropy and gray matter volume changes in Shidu parents: A five-year multimodal MRI study.
summary: People who have lost their only child (Shidu parents) may experience prolonged bereavement-related psychological trauma. Although structural brain alterations have been reported, whether baseline functional complexity is associated with subsequent gray matter volume (GMV) changes remains unclear. This study included 66 Shidu parents and 33 healthy controls. Five-year longitudinal structural MRI was used to assess GMV changes in Shidu parents, and baseline brain entropy (BEN) was derived from resting-state fMRI. title: From features to digital biomarkers: EEG-fNIRS classification pipelines for brain monitoring.
summary: Electroencephalography (EEG) and functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) are widely used for noninvasive brain monitoring in clinical and cognitive applications, where machine learning-based classification has become increasingly prevalent. Alongside algorithmic advances, a growing body of literature reports signal-derived metrics as digital biomarkers; however, their interpretation, validity, and comparability remain strongly dependent on target definition, processing pipelines, and evaluation practices. summary: Theory of Mind (ToM) develops from early reasoning about others' beliefs and intentions toward more advanced forms of recursive and socially embedded mental-state understanding. This ability emerges alongside the progressive maturation of large-scale brain networks. Here, we introduce a multidimensional neural maturity framework, derived from naturalistic functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI), that characterizes children's neurofunctional maturation along three dimensions: functional connectivity, temporal fluctuation, and spatial activation, by capturing neural responses to social narratives. summary: Children who are HIV-exposed but uninfected (HEU) are at increased risk of neurodevelopmental delays, yet neuroimmune pathways linking perinatal HIV exposure to school readiness remain unclear. title: 1H MRS reveals impact of early adversity and age on neurometabolic profiles in women.
summary: Exposure to early-life stress (ELS), including neglect or abuse, is known for its detrimental effects on brain health. This study investigated how ELS interacts with chronological age to impact on brain metabolism in middle-aged women using proton magnetic resonance spectroscopy (1H MRS) at 3 T. High-quality spectra from the hippocampus (HC) and posterior cingulate cortex (PCC) from 75 women, including 53% with ELS exposure before puberty, were analyzed. title: Enhanced functional connectivity in right precuneus after high-frequency repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation in Parkinson's disease patients with chronic musculoskeletal pain.
summary: Repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) can relieve chronic musculoskeletal pain (MSP) in Parkinson's disease (PD), yet the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. title: EEG Microstate Alterations and Their Association with Cognitive Performance in Late-Onset Epilepsy of Unknown Etiology: Comparison with Alzheimer's Disease.
summary: Cognitive impairment is common in late-onset epilepsy of unknown etiology (LOEU), but its electrophysiological correlates and relationship to Alzheimer's disease (AD) remain unclear. We compared resting-state electroencephalogram (EEG) microstate dynamics among LOEU, AD, and cognitively normal (CN) groups and examined their associations with cognitive performance. Eyes-closed 32-channel resting-state EEG recordings were analyzed from 60 patients with LOEU, 65 with AD, and 60 CN participants. Four canonical microstate classes (A-D) were identified. title: Altered directional brain-heart interactions across resting states and frequency bands in schizophrenia.
summary: Schizophrenia is associated with abnormalities in cortical activity and autonomic regulation, but directional brain-heart interaction (BHI) across resting states and frequency bands remains unclear. Resting-state electroencephalography (EEG) and electrocardiography (ECG) were recorded simultaneously in 33 medicated men with schizophrenia and 29 healthy men during eyes-open and eyes-closed conditions. Directional BHI was assessed across two coupling directions, two cardiac frequency components, and five EEG frequency bands. title: Longitudinal multimodal MRI correlates of subclinical insomnia symptoms and depressive mood in young adults.
summary: Insomnia symptoms and depressive mood often change together in young adults, but their longitudinal associations with diffusion tensor image analysis along the perivascular space (DTI-ALPS), an indirect index of perivascular-space diffusivity, and within-limbic functional connectivity remain unclear. 308 university students (233 women; age 19.0 ± 0.9 years) completed the Insomnia Severity Index (ISI), Self-Rating Depression Scale (SDS), diffusion MRI, and resting-state fMRI at baseline and after 1.7 ± 0.5 years. title: Spatial-Frequency-Dependent Temporal Dynamics of Orientation Ensemble Representation.
summary: Average representation refers to the rapid extraction of the central tendency from a set of stimuli by the visual system. However, whether this efficient process relies on specific spatial frequency (SF) information remains poorly understood. To investigate the roles of low spatial frequency (LSF) and high spatial frequency (HSF) information in orientation ensemble averaging and the underlying temporal dynamics, we conducted two experiments combining behavioral and electroencephalographic (EEG) measures. title: Silent cerebral ischemia after anticoagulation- or TEE-guided cardioversion: The randomized AFTER-CV trial.
summary: Silent cerebral ischemia after elective cardioversion is incompletely characterized, and randomized MRI-based evidence comparing anticoagulation-guided and transesophageal echocardiography (TEE)-guided pathways is limited. AFTER-CV was a prospective, randomized, open-label, parallel-group trial of 112 patients undergoing elective cardioversion, assigned 1:1 by sealed-envelope randomization to at least 3 weeks of therapeutic oral anticoagulation or a TEE-guided strategy. title: Simultaneous EEG - fMRI study of brain activity during the autobiographical memory task in depressed patients with suicidal ideation.
summary: Over-general autobiographical memory (OGM) refers to the tendency to recall personal experiences vaguely rather than as specific incidents. OGM serves as a significant risk factor for suicidal ideation in depressed patients and may represent a novel target for early warning and intervention. However, differences in neural function during autobiographical memory retrieval among depressed patients with suicidal ideation, depressed patients without suicidal ideation, and healthy controls remain incompletely understood. title: LifespanFix: Semi-supervised cortical correction across the human lifespan.
summary: Accurate characterization of the cerebral cortex in brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is essential for reliable morphometric analyses across the human lifespan. However, the cortex's thin and highly convoluted architecture, together with imaging artifacts, frequently introduces topological and anatomical defects in segmentation that can bias downstream analyses. Here we present LifespanFix, a lifespan-robust cortical correction model that directly fixes topological and anatomical defects in segmentation. title: Simultaneous EEG-fMRI in major depressive disorder: A systematic review of brain networks, neurovascular coupling, and clinical correlates.
summary: Simultaneous electroencephalography-functional magnetic resonance imaging (EEG-fMRI) offers unique potential to characterize brain network dysfunction and neurovascular coupling in major depressive disorder (MDD). However, the field lacks a rigorous synthesis restricted to strictly defined MDD populations with true multimodal integration. Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines (PROSPERO: CRD420261292902), we searched PubMed, Scopus, CENTRAL, and Google Scholar (inception to March 2026) for simultaneous EEG-fMRI studies in adults (≥18 years) with MDD. title: Graded and left-lateralized alterations in the diffusion tensor image analysis along the perivascular space index across major psychiatric disorders.
summary: Major depressive disorder (MDD), bipolar disorder (BD), and schizophrenia (SZ) show overlapping clinical and neurobiological features. We included 815 right-handed Chinese participants from two sites: 191 with MDD, 107 with BD, 327 with SZ, and 190 healthy controls (HC). title: Frontocentral theta oscillations bias perceptual judgments of ambiguous visual causality.
summary: Human perceptual decisions frequently rely on incomplete, ambiguous sensory inputs resolved prior to stimulus onset. Prior electrophysiological work confirms pre-event frontocentral ERP components predict ambiguous visual causal judgments, yet the spectrotemporal signatures of spontaneous oscillatory biases remain uncharacterized. Frontocentral theta signals proactive cognitive control, but whether pre-event theta oscillation modulates high-order causal inference independently of stimulus-locked ERPs remains untested. title: Clinical, radiological, and biomarker outcomes following a switch from MabThera® to the rituximab biosimilar Rixathon® in multiple sclerosis.
summary: Rituximab is widely used off-label for multiple sclerosis (MS) in Sweden, and many centres have transitioned from originator rituximab (MabThera®) to biosimilars for economic reasons. Evidence on outcomes following a switch to the biosimilar Rixathon® in MS remains limited. title: Serum NOX5: age-invariant increases in multiple sclerosis and associations with paramagnetic rim lesions.
summary: Multiple sclerosis (MS) misdiagnosis remains a clinical problem that lacks blood-based biomarkers. NADPH oxidase 5 (NOX5) is a human-specific marker of oxidative stress and vascular dysfunction; it has been suggested as a candidate biomarker. We aimed to evaluate serum NOX5 not just as a diagnostic discriminator for MS, but also define its relationship to MS clinical and imaging pathology. title: Perioperative management of patients with recent concussion undergoing noncardiac extracranial surgery: A modified Delphi consensus study.
summary: Many patients present for surgery soon after concussion, when cerebral physiologic regulation may remain disturbed, and no evidence-based guideline or standardized consensus recommendations exist. We sought expert consensus for adults with recent concussion undergoing noncardiac extracranial surgery. We conducted a two-round modified Delphi study (November 2025-March 2026). Round 1 items, drafted from a systematic literature search, included case vignettes. title: Potter-Optimized Multiscale Bayesian Gated Axial Quantized Attention Network for Robust Multichannel EEG-ECG-Based Seizure Prediction.
summary: Accurate seizure prediction from physiological signals remains challenging because electroencephalography (EEG)-ECG recordings contain substantial noise, nonlinear temporal patterns, inter-subject variability, and complex cross-modal dependencies. title: Neurobehavioral Assessment of ADHD and Anxiety Co-occurrence in Pediatric Populations.
summary: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is frequently comorbid with anxiety, a condition that complicates diagnosis and treatment. Stimulant medications used to treat ADHD may exacerbate anxiety in some children, although this is not a consistent effect. This study investigates Alpha Peak Frequency (APF) as a potential neurophysiological marker, alongside Theta/Beta Ratio (TBR) and Sensorimotor Rhythm (SMR), to compare children with ADHD alone (ADHD group) and those with ADHD and comorbid anxiety (COM group) using electrophysiological and behavioral assessments. title: A Pilot Study of the Neural Activation Associated with Convergence Subtypes in Individuals with Convergence Insufficiency.
summary: The purpose of this pilot investigation was to assess the neural correlates of convergence eye movement subtypes in individuals with convergence insufficiency using functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI). Data were gathered from six individuals with convergence insufficiency. Brain activation was assessed using fMRI while subjects made convergence eye movements in response to stimuli that primarily led to changes in: (1) accommodative convergence (monocular viewing through a -2.00 D lens), (2) proximal convergence (monocular viewing of Difference-of-Gaussian (DOG) targets at different distances) and (3) disparity convergence (step increases in the disparity of a random dot stereogram).

title: Pontine capillary telangiectasia in a patient with abducens nerve palsy.
summary: A 42-year-old woman presented with sudden-onset binocular diplopia and isolated right abducens nerve palsy. title: Structural brain changes in age-related macular degeneration before and 6 months after Scharioth macula lens implantation: an exploratory MRI study.

title: Associations between white matter network alterations and visuospatial and social-emotional deficits in patients with right hemisphere tumors: a prospective clinico-radiological study.
summary: Preserving neurological function is crucial in brain tumor surgery. Because the right hemisphere supports visuospatial and social‑cognitive abilities, damage may affect quality of life. summary: Acute symptomatic seizures (ASyS) account for nearly half of new onset seizures, but evidence guiding management remains limited. title: Scalp high-frequency oscillations differentiate neonates with hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy with and without electroencephalographically confirmed seizures.
summary: Hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy (HIE) is a leading cause of neonatal seizures, but seizure detection is challenging when continuous electroencephalography (EEG) is unavailable and neonates undergo only a single routine EEG. summary: The objective of the study was to assess epilepsy-related services across Italian neurology and child neuropsychiatry residency programs, evaluate residents and early-career specialists' perceived strengths/weaknesses in epilepsy training, and identify unmet needs and expectations for improving residency programs and Young Epilepsy Section (YES)-Italy educational initiatives. summary: Malignant hyperthermia (MH) is a rare, life-threatening reaction to certain anesthetic medications that can occur during surgery. title: Long-lasting somatosensory cortex dysfunction in some, but not all, individuals after sport-related concussion.
summary: Systems-level neurophysiologic dysfunction has been documented after acute sport-related concussion in multiple studies over the past quarter century. title: Wernicke Encephalopathy in Critical Illness: A Diagnostic Challenge With Evolving MRI Findings.
summary: Wernicke encephalopathy (WE) is an acute neurologic disorder caused by thiamine deficiency that can result in significant neurologic morbidity if not promptly recognized and treated. summary: To explore the associations of total screen time, smart device use, physical activity, and neuromuscular fitness with brain gray matter volumes in adolescence. summary: Delayed postischemic leukoencephalopathy (DPIL) is an under-recognized cause of delayed white matter injury following cerebral ischemia. title: Novel TUBB3 Variant p.Arg380Leu Is Associated with Brain Malformations Detectable by Neurosonography and Magnetic Resonance Imaging.
summary: Tubulinopathies are a heterogeneous group of congenital brain malformations caused by pathogenic variants in genes encoding tubulin proteins. summary: Physiological aging can alter the brain endothelial glycocalyx and blood-brain barrier (BBB), while experimental seizures independently engage galectin-3 (Gal-3) and inflammasome-associated inflammatory signaling. summary: Myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibody-associated disease (MOGAD) is an autoimmune inflammatory demyelinating disorder of the central nervous system with a broad clinical spectrum, although brainstem-predominant presentations in the elderly are rare and may closely mimic neoplastic lesions.
